column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to rise at night and has singular “the field”; BSB says “tonight” and plural “fields”.
The Hebrew uses “him” without repeating Gaal and says to do to him what your hand finds; BSB has “Gaal” and “do to them whatever you are able”.
The Hebrew calls them all the people; BSB calls them troops.
The Hebrew says they rose from the ambush, singular; BSB says they came out from their hiding places, plural.
The Hebrew specifies the heads of the mountains and has singular “shadow”; BSB uses plural “shadows”.
The Hebrew calls the center of the land its navel.
The Hebrew retains the image of the mouth; BSB gives its meaning as “gloating”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Gaal’s name or identify the fallen as Shechemites.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the people” without naming Shechem and actively narrates “they told Abimelech”.
The Hebrew says “the people”, not “his men”, and uses singular “the field”.
The Hebrew names the two companies without an explicit “other”.
The Hebrew repeats “the city” as the object of capturing and demolishing it; BSB uses pronouns.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names Abimelech twice and has plural “the axes”, singular “his hand”, and a separate action of lifting the branch.
The Hebrew narrates their dying rather than making killing a further action of the attackers.
The Hebrew repeats Thebez’s name; BSB uses a pronoun for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats “all” before the citizens of the city.
The Hebrew separately narrates arriving at the tower, fighting it, and approaching its entrance; BSB makes attacking the purpose of coming.
The Hebrew describes a piece of an upper millstone; BSB names an upper millstone without “a piece”.
The Hebrew calls him the young man carrying his equipment and later “his young man”; BSB uses armor-bearer and repeats Abimelech’s name.
The Hebrew says each man went to his place; BSB says they all went home.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular “their head”; BSB uses plural “their own heads”.
